passages.context: The complete final stanza, read with the preceding Sea of Faith stanza in the identified first-edition transcription. Lines 29–34 move from a plea that two lovers remain true to an accumulating neither/nor catalogue in which the world lacks love and consolation. The form and context support describing a strong structural and verbal echo or inversion of Romans 8:38–39; they do not establish conscious authorial dependence, quotation, or Arnold's intended biblical source.
passages.notes: The text preserves the TEI transcription's wording and punctuation while joining verse lines with spaces. Any consumer should distinguish the observable echo from a claim about Arnold's conscious borrowing.

work.author: Matthew Arnold
work.description: Matthew Arnold's lyric first published in New Poems (1867). Its final stanza turns from the retreating Sea of Faith to a plea for fidelity between lovers and a catalogue of what the apparently beautiful world lacks.
work.title: Dover Beach
